entities.name: André du Laurens
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
André du Laurens (1558–1609) was a French physician who rose to become premier médecin to King Henry IV and a leading academic doctor of late Renaissance France. Trained in the Galenic tradition yet alert to anatomical learning after Vesalius, he wrote widely circulated medical treatises on topics from ophthalmology to melancholy and general practice.

As royal physician du Laurens stood at the junction of court politics and learned medicine: advising the king, supervising health ritual, and lending prestige to Montpellier–Paris medical networks. His Latin works were translated and read across Europe, making him one of the more visible French medical authors around 1600.

He exemplifies the court-physician intellectual who translated humanist erudition into practical authority at the Bourbon monarchy’s founding moment.
